show_hn.title: Show HN: I wrote an email app that accepts only one sender per inbox
show_hn.story_text:
Infinite inboxes, including prefixes where you don't have to create inboxes before you use them -- they self create when you add a suffix. Three types of inboxes:
- One sender. Locks to the first domain to send email (except gmail, outlook, etc where it locks to an email account for obivous reasons. It bounces everyone else.
- Temporary. Lasts for a while (24h, 7days, etc) then bounces. Received messages stay or go as per your choice.
- Prefix. The most powerful. Declare a prefix like "service" and then invent any suffix, like "service-netflix" or "service$bank" and it creates a new one-sender inbox locked to whoever wrote first. Bring you own domain. Bring your own AI (MCP server ready). Forwarding. Please help me test it.

show_hn.story_text:
We noticed during the course of many many years of DBA related work that fixes to database issues and queries are always reactive. An entire database can fall over extremely quickly when an unbounded query grows without warning. Traditionally, DBAs hear complaints of slowness and follow a methodical process: 
- manually browse pg_stats or other database related performance internal tables 
- see which queries are slowest
- figure out what indexes are missing
- figure out which indexes are actually bad and slowing down writes
- painstakingly implement a fix In the age of cheap intelligence, we decided that there is no reason we can’t have an always-on agent that is designed to do this job for you.  Databases need something or someone that is always watching with a massive amount of contextu

show_hn.story_text:
Endo is a Higher-Order Harness (HOH). From the easiest concept to understand to the more complex ones, Endo gives you:
* A single, simple UI to use any agent provider with your existing subscriptions, and hot-swap agents right in the middle of a session.
* An orchestration layer, which I call HOH, allowing arbitrary composition of agents to achieve any workflow. A fun case I tried was asking Fable and Astra to mock a presidential debate.
* An agent protocol that abstracts any agent. The key insight here is that every LLM is an agent—instead of treating the LLM as just one node inside an external ReAct loop. Show HN: Run AI-generated logic safely inside your app
show_hn.story_text: Stof is an open-source runtime for logic you don't own or fully trust. Imagine a JSON document with functions inside, scoped to just the document that contains them. Stof instantiates this doc as a small wasm env, and makes these functions safe to call. They can't access or manipulate anything but their own doc. WebAssembly by itself is large in binary form, requires a lot of tooling, etc. Stof can be sent over the wire easily, is a superset of JSON for compatibility, and keeps the guarantees. I created Stof not to replace a data format or anything, but to be a glue layer for data and distributed systems to work with one another.
